newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT-NYMEX futures in consolidation, bias lower.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-NYMEX futures in consolidation, bias lower.

text.p: NEARBY MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI-14 * MA-10 * MA-20
* Brent and WTI are in short-term uptrend, but some indicators suggest the danger may have increased for the longs.
* An inverted head and shoulders pattern on the spot month unleaded gasoline chart is a potentially supportive pattern.
NYMEX crude and products futures are likely to continue to move sideways in consolidation today but with a little downside bias, analysts said.
"September WTI continues to hold, just about, its bullish uptrend," said Tom James at Credit Lyonnais Rouse in Singapore.

He said the daily September chart holds a key uptrend support drawn from the lows of July 15, August 8 and August 11, giving key support at $18.82 today, while on the spot month continuation chart it comes in at around $19.79.
However, Leslie Nicholas at GNI Research said in his daily report, "Brent and WTI are in short-term uptrend, but some indicators suggest the danger may have increased for the longs."".
But fundamentally he said, "U.S. refiner demand is good, helped by a cutback in Canadian shipments for September while the North Sea is influenced by the lower September loading programmes."

Slow stochastics have crossed over following Friday's weaker price action on the respective October Brent and September WTI contracts and WTI close below the 10-day moving average line, both factors that could be pointing crude prices lower, at least in the short term.
Analysts said these indicators may be countered by neutral RSIs across the complex, underlying chart support and relatively bullish fundamentals.

The fundamental strength of gasoline may continue to underpin the markets while technical momentum is slow with nearby chart support still intact with a supportive inverted head and shoulders pattern in place.

James pointed out the inverted head and shoulders pattern on the spot month unleaded gasoline chart, which he said "is a potentially supportive pattern given the previous bearish trend seen from the end of July."
The neckline of the head and shoulders pattern is drawn from the high of Aug 8 and Aug 12, the inverted head being the low hit on Aug 11.
James said, "The formation of the head and shoulders pattern certainly warns us not to get too bearish just yet on this product as there may be some hidden life in the contract".

Fenella Graham at MeesPierson Derivatives Ltd said, "Preparation is overall neutral, but maintains a bias to the long side so continue to buy the dips keeping a careful eye on gasoline as the support in the market".

Heating oil still looks fairly bullish longer term. Despite having broken below short term uptrend support the double bottom at 54.25 cents from last week remains intact as does longer term trendline support from June 20's 50.70 cents low which comes in at around 52.75 cents today.
To the upside trendline resistance is pegged around 55.60 cents.
-- Colin Wooster, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7456
